claim_bindings.downstream_scope: Internal legacy ID only; learner wording must use electron loss/gain and oxidation-number increase/decrease.
Class XI formal redox layer; not authorized by the Class X source alone.
Formal redox agent assignment after electron/oxidation-number tracking; rule is derived chemistry, not attributed verbatim to the exemplar index.

equation_bindings.downstream_scope: Reaction itself is a Class X foundation example; oxidation-number/agent annotations require FORMAL_G11 authority.

transformation_bindings.downstream_scope: Formal oxidising/reducing-agent assignment is Class XI scope; this fingerprint is a derived structural example, not a frozen NCERT question.
Grade XI only; illustrative derived example; must be SOURCE_SCOPE_HELD for Grade 9/10 learner products unless owner scope explicitly includes formal redox balancing.

scope_tiers.description: Recognise oxidation/reduction in NCERT Class X reaction examples using oxygen/hydrogen change and the supplied equation context.
Use electron transfer and oxidation-number changes to identify oxidation, reduction, oxidising agents and reducing agents.
Balance formal ionic redox systems and half-reactions, including acidic/basic medium when the request scope explicitly authorizes it.

preferred_surface_language: oxidation: electron loss / oxidation number increases
reduction: electron gain / oxidation number decreases
oxidising agent is reduced; reducing agent is oxidised

current_gate_defects.repair: The v1 gate cited Class X Section 1.2.5 as authority for oxidation-number rules, electron transfer and half-reaction balancing. The audit splits Class X foundation from Class XI formal redox authority.
The permanganate half-reaction transformation is now explicitly EXTENDED_G11 and cannot silently enter Grade 9/10 products.
Legacy mnemonic and architecture labels remain internal IDs only and are prohibited from learner-facing surfaces.
The NCERT Exemplar index is used only to establish the official Unit 8 practice corpus; specific derived equations or agent rules are not falsely attributed to that index.
